blocks.content: # EXIT-CVD: A European Initiative to Transform Cardiovascular Disease

blocks.title: About the Project
blocks.content:
EXIT-CVD is a five-year research project co-funded by the **European Union Innovative Health Initiative (IHI)** and industry partners, with a total budget of EUR 27.6 million. The research consortium is led by **University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG)** and **Philips**, and aims to transform how cardiovascular disease is detected, monitored and treated.
More than 60 million people in the European Union are living with cardiovascular disease. For many, the condition significantly reduces quality of life and well-being. Without early detection, timely diagnosis and appropriate treatment, cardiovascular disease can progress silently from early risk factors to established disease and ultimately, cardiac events that may lead to premature death.
EXIT-CVD identifies and acts on three key exit points along the cardiac care journey: preventing disease before it develops (early exit), reversing disease progression (mid exit), or halting progression in advanced stages (late exit).

blocks.title: The Role of Onsentia & RADAR-base
blocks.content:
Onsentia powers the digital data collection and remote monitoring infrastructure for EXIT-CVD using the open-source RADAR-base platform.
By combining active patient-reported outcome measurements (aRMT) with broad passive sensor and wearable data collection (pRMT), Onsentia and RADAR-base enable multi-source, scalable, real-time remote monitoring and data integration across modern clinical trials.
Onsentia participates in two studies in the "early exit": **COMPASS** and **EMPOWER-BP**.

blocks.title: COMPASS Study
blocks.content: Led by King's College London (KCL)/GSTT, the COMPASS study brings together unique technological capabilities from several partners. **Huawei Health** provides ambulatory blood pressure monitoring via its D3 Watch, which uses a novel integrated oscillometric wrist BP cuff. Onsentia's decentralised remote monitoring platform collects data from the Huawei D3 Watch. **MEGI** provides an AI-powered digital health app that delivers personalised cardiovascular and maternal heart care assessments, and **CogStack** assists in identifying participants from medical records.

blocks.title: EMPOWER-BP Study
blocks.content: Universitair Medisch Centrum Utrecht (UMCU), together with Universita' Di Pavia (UNIPV), Politecnico Di Milano (POLIMI) and Stichting Vrouwenhart, the EMPOWER-BP study utilises a citizen science approach, recruiting participants to Onsentia's platform and enabling remote self-enrolment via social media and the Huawei D3 Watch wearable. This study seeks to engage patients directly in their health management, enhancing adherence and reducing healthcare costs.

blocks.title: More Information
blocks.content:
For more details about the EXIT-CVD project, visit [exitcvd.eu](https://exitcvd.eu/).
This website is hosted by King's College London on its secure health research platform called RADAR-base.
